clinical_knowledge.topic: Basal Cell Carcinoma evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Basal Cell Carcinoma is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC), nodular subtype, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Basal Cell Carcinoma.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Squamous cell carcinoma without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Missing facial numbness, weakness, fixation, or a new neck lump, which warrants prompt specialist assessment for more extensive disease.

teaching.one_liner: Most common non-melanoma skin cancer presenting as a translucent, pearly papule with telangiectasias.

must_ask.say: Did this skin bump start as a smooth pearly nodule with visible tiny blood vessels?
Does the lesion bleed easily when touched or develop a central crust that doesn't heal?
Do you have a history of significant sun exposure or outdoor work?
How slowly has this lesion expanded over recent time?
Have you noticed facial numbness or weakness, a fixed sore, or any new lump in your neck or under your jaw?

history.answer: I have this small bump on my right cheek that just won't heal, and it bleeds whenever I wash my face.
I first noticed a tiny bump about 6 months ago, and it has stayed there ever since.
It is located right on the middle of my right cheek.
It started out tiny like a small pimple, but it has been slowly and steadily growing over the last 6 months.
It's about the size of a pencil eraser, maybe 5 or 6 millimeters across, and it's the only one like this.
It feels slightly firm when I touch it, not soft or squishy, and it doesn't move around freely under the skin.
No, it doesn't hurt at all, and it's not tender even when I press right on it.
It looks like a raised, pearly-white or shiny bump, and I can see tiny little red veins on the surface.
Yes, it bleeds easily if I scrape it or pat it with a towel, then it crusts over for a bit, but it never fully heals.
No, there is no redness around it, no warmth, and no pus or foul-smelling fluid draining from it.
No, there is no central dark pore or hole, and nothing cheesy or white ever comes out of it.
No, it doesn't fluctuate or change size. It just stays raised and gradually gets larger.
No, I have never had any cut, injury, surgery, or bad acne in that spot.
history.topic: Prior trauma or scar at site

history.answer: No, I haven't had any fever, night sweats, unexplained weight loss, or swollen glands in my neck.
I worked outdoors as a farmer for more than forty years in the direct sun, rarely used sunscreen or hats, and had several blistering sunburns when I was younger.
I have never had skin cancer diagnosed before, and no one in my family has had skin cancer or unusual moles.
history.topic: Personal and family skin cancer history

history.answer: No, I have never taken medications that suppress the immune system, never had an organ transplant, and I don't have diabetes.
Early on I thought it was a stubborn pimple and tried squeezing it, but only a drop of clear fluid and blood came out, so I left it alone.
No, my face feels completely normal with no numbness, tingling, or weakness in my facial muscles.
At first I thought it was just an irritated pimple or a harmless sun spot, but with the bleeding and growth, I'm really worried it might be skin cancer.
I would like to have a small piece taken for testing, and I'd like to get the whole thing removed if possible.
Aside from having a lot of weathered, sun-damaged skin from farming, I don't have any major medical illnesses.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter pills, or herbal supplements.
I have no known allergies to any medications or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I only have a small glass of beer once or twice a month, if that.
I am a retired farmer and I live quietly at home with my wife.
My parents lived into their eighties and died of natural causes, and my siblings are healthy with no history of tumors or skin cancer.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 122/76 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.6 °C, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Well-appearing older man in no acute distress, with prominent solar lentigines and weathered, sun-damaged skin across the face and neck.

Single 6 mm discrete, raised, pearly-white translucent nodule on the right mid-cheek with rolled borders, surface telangiectasias, and a tiny central scab, nontender and mobile over deep facial structures.
No palpable lymphadenopathy in the preauricular, postauricular, submandibular, or cervical lymph node chains bilaterally.
Facial sensation to light touch is intact bilaterally across all three trigeminal divisions, and facial expressions are symmetric without weakness.
Pupils equal, round, and reactive to light, extraocular eye movements fully intact, and the cheek lesion does not impinge on the lower eyelid margin.
